conviction_note: Q3 revenue and cash were pre-announced on 15 Oct, so tonight turns on what the update left out. The Q4 positive-EBITDAS target that the Q2 release called 'on track' is missing from it. The 'record low' $28m Q3 cash use includes about $47m of asset-sale cash received in July and August, while the company presented the figure as fundamental improvement. A $275-287m Q4 implied by the reaffirmed guide also has to hold. The documented negatives sum to -2.6, but short interest is 21.9% of float, the options book is call-heavy and fuel-cell names rallied into the print, so p_up sits at 45, not lower, on an 8% absolute move. That gives -0.8. The symposium on 19 Nov (outside the window) may hold the 2027 story, which is why the move is set below the 12.4% option-implied move.
bar: Disputed. Q3 revenue consensus is $192.6m on Benzinga (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/PLUG/earnings-forecasts) and $202.85m from 17 analysts on FXEmpire (https://www.fxempire.com/stocks/plug/earnings). The company's own pre-announcement says Q3 revenue grew >10% on Q3 2025's $177.1m, so above $194.8m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001093691/000110465926115964/tm2627628d1_ex99-1.htm). EPS consensus is -$0.06 on both sources. The FY2026 guide is +15-16% on FY2025's ~$710m, about $816-823m (Q2 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001093691/000110465926093339/tm2622713d1_ex99-1.htm). Because the revenue bar is disputed, every finding that depends on it is capped small. The revenue number is pre-announced, so print_vs_bar is about -1% against a ~$197m midpoint.
positioning_check: Short interest 291.96m shares (previous month 284.62m), 21.89% of float, 5.86 days to cover. Source: stockanalysis.com statistics, page checked 2026-11-09 (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/plug/statistics). Equibles showed 21.0% of float and 6.0 days as of 2026-08-20. This is a crowded short. The baseline has no 25-delta skew (null). Put/call open-interest ratio is 0.08, so the front expiry is overwhelmingly calls. ATM IV is 146.9% and the event-implied move 12.44%. Run-up is +14.1% over 5 days, -7.7% over 20 days, and the stock is 64% below its 52-week high. The 5-day bounce matches a sector rally in fuel-cell names on AI data-centre power demand (+5% on 6 Nov, https://www.kapitalmarktexperten.de/plug-power-aktie-rechenzentren-rueckenwind/). Every negative below was shrunk for the squeeze risk.

findings.finding: The 'record low' Q3 net cash use of ~$28m (unrestricted cash $161.9m on 30 Jun to ~$134m on 30 Sep) includes the ~$47m of asset-sale proceeds the Q2 release said arrived in July and August. On a like-for-like basis the burn is ~$75m against ~$61m in Q2, worse, not better. The 15 Oct update said the $28m 'reflects overall operating results and fundamental improvement' and mentioned only the absence of ATM proceeds. Tonight's 10-Q cash-flow statement will show the asset-sale inflow, and its subsequent-events note will show whether any of the $944m ATM capacity was used after 30 Sep, with the stock at $1.3-1.5.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: PLUG rose +2.76% on 15 Oct when the $28m 'record low' burn was first published (baseline). A peer shows how this line is being treated now: Bloom Energy beat and raised guidance on 22 Oct 2026 and still fell ~9-11% on negative operating cash flow (https://www.trefis.com/stock/be/articles2/620854/why-did-bloom-energy-stock-jump/2026-10-27).
findings.why_not_priced: The headline everyone carried was 'record low $28m cash burn' (German retail press repeated it unqualified through 9 Nov), and the company framed it as operational. If the market had netted out the asset-sale cash, the stock would not have bounced on 15 Oct and the 'Cash-Burn' previews would not call the burn improved. Underlying burn of ~$75m against $134m of unrestricted cash is under two quarters of runway before further asset sales.
findings.independence: Shares two documents with nothing else: the Q2 8-K for the ~$47m received in Jul-Aug, and the 15 Oct 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001093691/000110465926115964/tm2627628d1_ex99-1.htm) for the $28m and $134m. The Graham asset-sale terms ($50m at closing, closing expected by 31 Jul) are in a separate document, the 13 Jul 2026 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926082854/tm2620282d1_8k.htm).

findings.finding: The 15 Oct business update does not mention EBITDAS or EBITDA at all. In the Q2 release (10 Aug) the company said it was 'on track to achieve its positive EBITDAS target in the fourth quarter of 2026', and the March FY2025 release said the same. Q4 is the quarter the target falls in, so tonight the company either reaffirms or walks back the main Project Quantum Leap milestone.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The milestone narrative has paid: +23.2% on 2 Mar 2026 (first positive gross margin, 'on track for positive EBITDAS by Q4 2026'), +5.2% on 10 Aug 2026 (guide raised, EBITDAS 'on track'). A walk-back has never been tested.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews and the German retail press restate the Q4 EBITDAS target as if it were current. If the omission were priced, the 5-day run-up would not be +14% into the call and the options book would not be 92% calls. This is an inference from silence, so it is sized small. Reaffirming would turn it positive, which is why the range is wide.
findings.independence: The Q2 8-K wording 'on track to achieve its positive EBITDAS target in Q4 2026' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001093691/000110465926093339/tm2622713d1_ex99-1.htm) is the comparison. This finding shares the 15 Oct document with the gross-margin wording finding: they are two different lines in one release.

findings.finding: The FY2026 guide reaffirmed on 15 Oct (+15-16% on ~$710m, so $816-823m) means Q4 2026 revenue of roughly $274-287m, given H1 of $341.8m and Q3 of ~$195-200m. That is +22-27% y/y on Q4 2025's $225.2m and ~+40% q/q. There is precedent: Q4 2025 was itself +27% q/q. Even so, a trim tonight would be a guidance cut.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide was raised on 10 Aug (+5.2%) and reaffirmed on 15 Oct (+2.8%). The name has not cut guidance in the baseline's eight prints.
findings.why_not_priced: The arithmetic is public. The company reaffirmed with two weeks of Q4 visibility, and the outcome sits inside its own guide, so this is sized near zero. It is filed because electrolyzer deliveries are lumpy: the Arcadia 280 MW deliveries start only after notice to proceed, and ENDOR has no FID.
findings.independence: Q4 2025 revenue of $225.2m comes from the FY2025 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465926022247/tm267677d1_ex99-1.htm). Q1 2026 ($163.5m) and Q2 ($178.3m) come from the Q1 and Q2 8-Ks.

findings.finding: The stock fell from about $2.5 (late June) to about $1.95 (late September), roughly 20%. Plug carries $136.3m of warrant liabilities and $578m of convertible notes at fair value (30 Jun 10-Q), and recorded $103.5m of fair-value losses on them in Q2 when the stock rose. The same remeasurement should run the other way in Q3, a non-cash gain of very roughly $100m+. That would narrow GAAP net loss sharply against Q2's ~$190m and could put headline GAAP EPS well above the -$0.06 consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 GAAP EPS of -$0.18 included ~$140m of non-cash convertible and warrant charges, and the stock still rose (+1.1%), so it trades on operations, not on the remeasurement. One-off: sized at a fraction.
findings.why_not_priced: EPS consensus of -$0.06 on 17 analysts (FXEmpire) looks like an operating estimate and not a fair-value-adjusted one. The value is a headline-algo beat in the first minutes, which the session close usually fades. Price levels come from secondary pages (Nasdaq first-half article; massive.com 26 Oct quote), so the gain size is an inference.
findings.independence: Q2 8-K lists the Q2 fair-value losses: convertible -$74.2m, warrants -$29.3m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001093691/000110465926093339/tm2622713d1_ex99-1.htm).

findings.finding: The 15 Oct update changes how gross margin is described. The Q2 release reported Q2 at ~breakeven against ~(13%) in Q1, a sequential claim. The 15 Oct update says margin 'improved over the past two quarters' and expects Q3 progress only 'year-over-year', and Q3 2025 was about -68% GAAP. That bar would be met even if Q3 margin slipped back below Q2's ~-1%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gross margin is the line this stock has paid for: +23.2% on 2 Mar 2026 when Q4 2025 printed the first positive gross margin (+2.4%). A slip back to negative after Q4 2025 +2.4% and Q2 ~-1% has not been tested.
findings.why_not_priced: Wording inference only. The company often frames margins year over year (the Q1 2026 headline was '71% margin improvement y/y'), so it is sized small. If the market read it as a Q3 margin step back, the stock would not have run +14% in five days into the print.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 GAAP gross loss of ~$120m on $177m revenue is in the Q3 2025 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1093691/000110465925109120/tm2530762d1_ex99-1.htm). This finding shares the 15 Oct document with the EBITDAS finding, on a different line.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print: 21.9% of float short with 5.86 days to cover, a front-expiry put/call open-interest ratio of 0.08 (heavily call-skewed open interest), and a +14% 5-day bounce on a sector-wide fuel-cell/data-centre rally (+5% on 6 Nov) with no Plug-specific news.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The big upside reaction (+23.2%, Mar 2026) came on a milestone into a heavily shorted tape. Downside reactions in the baseline were at most -10% (May 2025).
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest and the option book are themselves the price, so this is mostly priced. The residual is asymmetric squeeze fuel if the EBITDAS target is reaffirmed. Most of the crowded-short effect has already been applied by shrinking the negatives above, so this is kept small.
findings.independence: Sector rally: https://www.kapitalmarktexperten.de/plug-power-aktie-rechenzentren-rueckenwind/ (2026-11-06). Put/call OI comes from the sealed baseline.

findings.finding: COO Dean Fullerton resigned on 17 Sep, effective 23 Oct, to join another company, with duties passed to EVPs and VPs (8-K item 5.02). Plug then appointed Dr. Lee Sweetland, former Ballard COO, to lead global industrialization of PEM stacks. The call may cover the operations handover in the quarter the cost-out is meant to land.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline print on a management change. The 2025 president exit coincided with a fall, per a Yahoo headline whose date is unconfirmed.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for seven weeks and filed 'not due to any disagreement'. Almost fully priced and kept at near zero.

findings.finding: The New York Gateway sale to Stream US Data Centers was restructured on 9 Jul. The price is fixed at $142.0m, an interim closing of the real property is allowed, Stream adds a $10m deposit, and the outside closing date is 31 Mar 2027. The company has collected ~$52m of its $275m asset-monetization target. An interim or final Gateway closing or a dated timetable on the call would roughly double unrestricted cash ($134m) and answer the runway question in the cash finding.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The asset-sale announcement on 13 Jul 2026 (bmo) drew -2.69% (baseline). The market has not paid for monetization promises, only for receipts.
findings.why_not_priced: What the money buys is runway without the ATM at $1.4, which avoids dilution. That is a positive or zero, not distress. No closing has been announced, so it only pays if the call gives a date or reports an interim close. Sized small.
findings.independence: The $275m target and ~$52m collected are in the Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001093691/000110465926093339/tm2622713d1_ex99-1.htm).

findings.finding: Plug signed a 280 MW GenEco electrolyzer supply agreement for Arcadia eFuels' ENDOR e-SAF project in Denmark on 29 Sep, plus preferred-supplier status on >1 GW. ENDOR has an EU Innovation Fund grant and a Uniper offtake but no FID, so deliveries wait for notice to proceed. Orica's 50 MW order followed its FID in July. These support the 'second-half weighted' and 2027 pipeline story on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Orica order in July drew +1.5% pre-market. Order announcements have moved the stock little.
findings.why_not_priced: Public and mostly priced. The residual is whether the call converts the $8bn 'funnel' into a reported backlog number. Neither the 15 Oct update nor the Q2 release disclosed backlog.
findings.independence: Uniper offtake for ENDOR, KGAL release 25 Sep 2026 (https://www.pv-magazine.de/unternehmensmeldungen/kgal-espf-6-projekt-endor-schliesst-langfristigen-e-kerosin-abnahmevertrag-mit-uniper/).

outside_window.finding: The Plug Symposium 2026 ('Resilient Energy, Real Solutions'), 19 Nov 9:00-12:00 ET, is where management says it will set out business priorities. Any 2027 framework or data-centre strategy may be held for it, not for the call, which shrinks tonight's move.
Ballard Power (a peer) reports Q3 2026 on 16 Nov.
Gateway sale outside closing date is 31 Mar 2027, at $142.0m.

baseline_tension: The documented items lean negative: the cash burn flattered by asset-sale proceeds, the Q4 EBITDAS target missing from the 15 Oct update, and the Q4 revenue ramp. That runs against the +14% 5-day bounce, a call-heavy book and a 21.9%-of-float short. p_up is held at 45, not ~38, and each negative was shrunk for the squeeze. The 12.4% implied move is far above the name's 2.7% median reaction, and with the quarter pre-announced and the symposium after the window, abs_move is set at 8.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (crowded short, 21.9% of float, 5.86 days to cover): shrank the negatives, cash-quality -2.5 to -2.0, EBITDAS omission -2.0 to -1.5, gross-margin wording -1.0 to -0.7.
Core table and rule 7, no double application: the positioning finding cut from +1.5 to +0.5, because the squeeze effect was already applied by shrinking the negatives.
Rule 2 (one-offs as one-offs): the fair-value remeasurement gain cut from +0.8 to +0.5.
Rule 6 (disputed revenue bar, $192.6m vs $202.85m): the Q4-ramp guidance finding kept capped at -0.5 because it sits inside the reaffirmed guide; print_vs_bar unchanged.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the Gateway sale signed positive, since it buys runway without ATM dilution; unchanged.
Rule 1: reaction history shows margin and EBITDAS milestones have paid (+23.2%), so those findings were not shrunk further.
p_up moved from 44 to 45 for the crowded short; abs_move unchanged at 8.
